citation: An Act to reduce and fix the military peace establishment of the United States, ch. 13, 2 March 1821; United States Statutes at Large, vol. 3, p. 615
describes_date: the peace establishment in force from 1 June 1821
rights_note: An Act of Congress, printed in the official Statutes at Large. Edicts of government are not copyrightable in the United States.
note: Read for T-1349. Section 2 fixes what a company of infantry consisted of: 'each of which shall consist of one captain, one first lieutenant, one second lieutenant, three sergeants, four corporals, two musicians, and forty-two privates.' This is the law of the peace establishment on the scene date; the project has read no act between it and 1 July 1835 that moves an infantry company's strength, and if one exists it retires the reading. THE ESTABLISHMENT IS NOT A RETURN — it says what a company was authorised to hold, never how many men were present for duty at any post.
